rationale: This is a third-leg bolt-on to the archived "Liquidity-Induced Research Retrenchment" (identical first two legs) rather than a new mechanism, and stacking a third MIN mostly shrinks and destabilizes the extreme portfolio without addressing why that signal's cross-sectional slope was flat.

Substituting a lagged R&D-per-employee *state* and a three-year cost-ratio *trend* for the archived one-year delta-on-delta construction is a defensible persistence-based reframing with a coherent sign, though it remains adjacent to the existing "R&D Process-Efficiency Payoff" and to well-known gross-margin-trend profitability effects.

This is a near-mechanical restatement of the archived "Goodwill-Backed Physical Productivity" (same goodwill scaler, same gross-profit-over-gross-PPE payoff leg) with only the ratio-growth replaced by a scaled first difference, which is a cosmetic denominator fix rather than a different economic test.

Measuring gross-profit change against the *prior* period's combined capex and R&D outlay is a genuine timing and payoff-metric change relative to the earlier contemporaneous sales-growth-over-investment ratios, and it directly targets the sign conflict those produced, though the small, occasionally near-zero denominator makes it fragile even after winsorization.

This simply swaps the second leg of the archived "Customer-Capital Inventory Conversion" for the sale/cogs growth term already used in "R&D-Backed Pricing Power," and because COALESCE(xad,0) forces the product to exactly zero for the large non-disclosing majority, the industry rank is dominated by a huge tied mass and the effective test is confined to a thin advertising subsample.

This appends a cost-efficiency leg to the archived "Equity-Funded R&D Deployment" without diagnosing why that signal was economically negligible, and a triple MIN of ranks makes the short leg an incoherent mixture of firms failing any one of three unrelated criteria.
